newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Podravka expects return to profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Podravka expects return to profit in 1997.

text.p: Croatia's leading food-processing group Podravka said on Thursday it expected to return to profit this year after completing financial consolidation.
"Last year we got rid of loss-making subsidiaries...and had some financial restructuring," board president Zvonimir Majdancic told a news conference.

Podravka posted a 135 million kuna loss in 1995 although its core business was profitable. But Majdancic expected the company to gradually improve its performance and reach a high profitability ratio of 10 percent of its sales by year 2005.
He said Podravka had sold four non-core businesses and liquidated another. It also substituted some 100 million kuna of old loans for cheaper ones and was seeking to lower all costs.
"Even in 1996 our core business and Belupo (pharmaceutical unit) were positive," Majdancic said.
He could not yet provide precise results for last year, but said Podravka increased production and sales of all leading products.
It is most famous in Croatia and central and eastern European markets for its food seasoning product Vegeta as well as instant soups and powdered baby food.
It recorded a 2.0-percent increase in the output of these leading products in 1996 while the mineral water and pharmaceutical production stagnated and fruit, vegetable and meat processing declined.
Exports, that account for some 30 percent of all sales, rose to $130 million in 1996 from around $50 million back in 1990.
Podravka's share price has risen steadily in the past few weeks to hit a record 375 kuna on Tuesday on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, but it closed at 330 kuna on Thursday.
